question.text: `Bharat Cements Ltd` reports the following for FY 2024-25: net worth INR 480 crore, turnover INR 1,200 crore, net profit INR 4.5 crore. Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, is CSR applicability triggered?

answer.text: No — all three thresholds must be breached simultaneously
No — net profit is below INR 5 crore, which is the controlling threshold
Yes — any ONE of the three thresholds (net worth ≥ INR 500 cr, turnover ≥ INR 1,000 cr, net profit ≥ INR 5 cr) triggers applicability, and turnover crosses INR 1,000 cr
Yes — but only voluntarily, since net worth and net profit are below the statutory levels

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135(1) triggers CSR applicability if a company, in the immediately preceding financial year, meets ANY ONE of: net worth ≥ INR 500 cr, turnover ≥ INR 1,000 cr, OR net profit ≥ INR 5 cr. `Bharat Cements` has turnover of INR 1,200 cr (≥ 1,000 cr), so CSR is mandatory — 2% of 3-year average net profit must be spent. The Trap: Option A reverses the OR into an AND (common trap). Option C overweights the net-profit limb — but any one limb alone is enough. Option D treats it as voluntary, but once a threshold is crossed, CSR is statutory. Cross-Exam Context: V-A (MF Distributor) and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser) test donor-side 80G deduction; XXIII tests the *company-side* CSR trigger. The 2% spend rate is the same across exams — only the applicability framing changes. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When your SE client is funded by a company's CSR, verify the donor's Section 135 applicability from their annual report before accepting the engagement — if the company is not actually CSR-liable, any 'CSR grant' shown in the SE books may be miscategorised and will trip up your Annual Impact Report reconciliation.
